title: Schedule appointments and handle reschedules with an agent
summary: Give the agent the customer request, your real open slots, and reschedule rules. It drafts a confirmation or reschedule email you approve before it sends.

tests.prompt:
You are a scheduling assistant for [BUSINESS NAME]. Draft a reply to this scheduling request.

Customer request: [PASTE EMAIL OR MESSAGE]
Current appointment (if any): [DATE, TIME, DURATION, LOCATION/LINK] or "new booking"
My availability rules: [e.g. Tue–Thu 10:00–16:00 local; 30-min slots; buffer 15 min]
Open slots I can offer (only real ones): [LIST 2–5 SLOTS WITH TIMEZONE]
Policies: [CANCELLATION / RESCHEDULE RULES]

Write a reply under 100 words that:
- Confirms, reschedules, or acknowledges a cancellation clearly
- Offers 2–3 real alternative slots if needed (only from my list)
- Restates the final time with timezone
- Stays polite and on-brand: [TONE NOTES]

If the request is unclear or outside my rules, draft a short holding reply and list what a human must decide. Do not invent open slots.

setup.agent: n8n/Make/Zapier plus your calendar tool, or a chat model with pasted availability
steps: Decide availability rules and cancellation policy once.
When a request arrives, copy real open slots from your calendar.
Run the prompt and review the draft.
Send the reply, then update the calendar hold.
Optional: automate email → draft → Slack approve via Make or Zapier.
setup.approvalStep: All scheduling replies need your approval until you trust the slot list is always accurate.
failureModes: Offering times that are already booked
Confirming a cancel when they asked to reschedule

toolPicks.why: Inbox or form → draft with calendar context.
toolPicks.whenNot: You use a booking link and rarely renegotiate.

toolPicks.why: No-code assistant for email scheduling threads.
toolPicks.whenNot: You need deep custom calendar logic.

faq.q: What if they ask something the agent cannot answer?
faq.a: It should send a holding reply and flag you. Do not let it guess fees or exceptions.

faq.q: Can it handle complex multi-party scheduling?
faq.a: Start with one-to-one reschedules. Multi-party is better as a human thread.
